Administracion de Aeropuertos y Servicio.desc: A Bolivian state body that planned, ran and administered the country's public airports and organised national airspace and air traffic control. Supreme Decree 8019 of 21 June 1967 set it up as a state organism depending administratively on the Ministry of Public Works and Communications, taking over Lloyd Aereo Boliviano's aeronautical infrastructure. Supreme Decree 4630 of 30 November 2021 ordered it to stop operating and be wound up.

sources.title: Decreto Supremo No 8019 de 21 de junio de 1967
Bolivia: Decreto Supremo No 4630, 30 de noviembre de 2021

Administradora Boliviana de Carreteras (.desc: The Bolivian state body responsible for planning and managing the Red Vial Fundamental, the national trunk road network. Law 3507 of 27 October 2006 set it up as an autonomous public-law entity with its own legal personality and assets, under the oversight of the Ministry of Public Works, Services and Housing. It also runs tolls, weighbridges and vehicle-dimension checks on that network, with 30 per cent of that revenue going to the departmental prefectures.

sources.title: Bolivia: Ley No 3507, 27 de octubre de 2006

NAABOL.desc: Navegacion Aerea y Aeropuertos Bolivianos (NAABOL), the Bolivian state body created by Supreme Decree 4630 of 30 November 2021, the decree that also wound up AASANA. It sits under the Ministry of Public Works, Services and Housing and is responsible for planning aeronautical infrastructure, running the state's airports, and organising airspace and air traffic control.

sources.title: Bolivia: Decreto Supremo No 4630, 30 de noviembre de 2021

Consejo Indigena del Pueblo Tacana (CIPT.desc: The representative organisation of the Tacana indigenous people in Abel Iturralde province, La Paz department, Bolivia, founded in 1993. It is run by a directorio with a president, vice-president and secretariats for natural resources, land and autonomy, education, health and communication. With the women's council CIMTA it represents the Tacana I communal territory, 20 communities across the municipalities of Ixiamas and San Buenaventura, and follows the territory's titling and its territorial management plans.

CONDER - Companhia de Desenvolvimento Ur.desc: A public company (empresa publica) of the Brazilian state of Bahia, listed as such on the register of state public companies kept by Bahia's commercial registry, JUCEB. A state decree makes it the body that carries out works and extensions on state public buildings once their cost passes limits set for each secretariat, and Bahia state Law 13.204 of 2014 allows the state administration secretariat to delegate the building of public facilities to it.

SEDUR - Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Ur.desc: A secretariat of the government of the Brazilian state of Bahia, based in the state administrative centre in Salvador. Bahia state Law 13.204 of 11 December 2014 gives it the purpose of drawing up and carrying out state policy on urban development, housing and technical assistance to municipalities, and creates within it a Superintendencia de Mobilidade for urban and interurban transport policy and a Superintendencia de Planejamento e Gestao Territorial, which also handles state solid-waste policy.

Committee for Roads of the Republic of K.desc: A committee inside the Kazakh ministry that holds roads, named over the years as a committee of the Ministry of Investments and Development, of the Ministry of Industry and Infrastructure Development and of the Ministry of Transport. It is the state body for public roads of international and national significance, and it plans and sets the strategic direction for road work, including approving the yearly investment plan of the national road operator.

KazAvtoZhol.desc: A state-owned joint stock company in Kazakhstan, KazAvtoZhol National Company JSC, which acts as the national operator of the main national road network, including international transit roads. Its annual investment plan has to be approved by the Roads Committee, and it collects road tolls through its KazToll portal.

sources.title: Transport Resilience and Connectivity Enhancement Project, project document

Department of Public Works and Highways.desc: A department of the Philippine national government. Its mandate, under section 3 of Executive Order 124 of 1987, is the planning, design, construction and maintenance of infrastructure, especially national highways, flood control and water resource development systems. Below the Office of the Secretary it has undersecretaries and assistant secretaries, bureaus, regional offices in Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao, and a Unified Project Management Office.

Hanoi People's Committee.desc: The executive body of Hanoi's People's Council and the city's state administrative authority. Under Vietnam's 2015 Law on Organization of Local Administration a People's Committee is elected by the People's Council at the same level and answers to that council and to higher administrative agencies; it is made up of a chairperson, vice chairpersons and members, and Hanoi may have up to five vice chairpersons. As the committee of a centrally run city it carries out council decisions on land use and urban planning and builds and manages urban infrastructure.

sources.title: Law No. 77/2015/QH13 on Organization of Local Administration
sources.publisher: National Assembly of Vietnam (English translation, LuatVietnam)

Hanoi Department of Transport.desc: A specialised agency of the Hanoi People's Committee. Under the committee's Decision 17/2008/QD-UBND of 29 September 2008 it advises and assists the committee in state management of transport in the city, covering roads, waterways and urban railways. The People's Committee directs its organisation, staffing and activities, while the Ministry of Transport guides it on technical matters.

sources.title: Hanoi Urban Railway Construction Project, preparatory survey report

TRAMOC (Hanoi Public Transport Managemen.desc: A unit under the Hanoi Department of Transport, established by Hanoi People's Committee Decision 2279/QD-UBND of 31 May 2007 to assist the department in managing public transport in the city. Its remit covers bus services: planning the city's bus network, managing bus infrastructure, coordinating bus operations, printing and issuing bus tickets, managing subsidy and fare revenue, and signing and monitoring contracts with bus operators.

sources.title: Hanoi Urban Railway Construction Project, preparatory survey report

Development Organization for the Rural P.desc: A Bangladeshi national non-governmental organisation, which gives its own name as Development Organisation of the Rural Poor. It works with poor women, children and excluded communities across fields including water and sanitation, microfinance and women's empowerment. Its own site says it operates in 31 upazilas across 19 districts, has more than 500 staff and more than 50 workplaces, and an annual turnover of over 22 crore taka.

sources.publisher: Development Organisation of the Rural Poor (DORP)

Electricity Generation Company of Bangla.desc: A Bangladeshi state electricity generation company under the Power Division of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources. It was incorporated on 23 November 1996 as Meghnaghat Power Company Limited and renamed Electricity Generation Company of Bangladesh Limited on 16 February 2004. It is a public limited company whose shares are not publicly traded, and its 2023 annual report gives its generation capacity as 954 MW across three plants.

sources.title: Annual Report 2023 (draft)
sources.publisher: Electricity Generation Company of Bangladesh Ltd

Gas Transmission Company Limited (GTCL).desc: A Bangladeshi state-owned company that operates the country's high-pressure gas transmission pipelines; it began in June 1993 with a 188 km north-south pipeline from Kailashtila to Ashuganj. It is one of the subsidiary companies of Petrobangla, the state oil, gas and mineral corporation, under the Ministry of Energy, Power and Mineral Resources. Its revenue was more than 22.67 billion taka in the 2024-25 financial year.

Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB).desc: The company that carries high-voltage electricity across Bangladesh, wheeling power from Bangladesh Power Development Board stations and other generators to the distribution utilities for a charge set by the Bangladesh Electricity Regulatory Commission. It was formed as a public limited company under Bangladesh's Companies Act, with the state-owned Bangladesh Power Development Board among the subscribers to its memorandum of association signed in November 1996, and its shares trade on the Chittagong Stock Exchange. Its network included 2,407 circuit km of 400 kV line and 8,445 circuit km of 132 kV line as of March 2024. It was renamed Power Grid Bangladesh PLC by a resolution of 10 February 2024.

Ghana Water Company Limited (GWCL).desc: Ghana's urban water utility, a wholly state-owned limited liability company responsible for producing, transmitting and distributing water in urban areas. It was created on 1 July 1999 by converting the Ghana Water and Sewerage Corporation, which Parliament had set up by Act 310 of 1965, under the Statutory Corporations (Conversion to Companies) Act 461 of 1993 as amended by LI 1648. The state's holding agency, SIGA, lists it as 100 per cent state-owned.

Maîtrise d'Ouvrage de l'Aéroport de Dons.desc: A Burkinabe public project-owner body set up to build the new Ouagadougou-Donsin airport, headed by a director general appointed by the Council of Ministers. Its 2019 tender documents were issued under the Prime Minister's Office, and the airport project was moved to the Ministry of Transport in April 2022. In June 2025 the Council of Ministers created a state company, the Societe des Aeroports du Faso, which takes over MOAD's functions along with those of two other aviation bodies.

Intercontinental Consultants and Technoc.desc: An Indian engineering consultancy, incorporated in 1987 as a private limited company and started in New Delhi. Highways and roads are its main line of work; it also covers bridges and tunnels, traffic and road safety, rail and metro, aviation, urban planning, water resources and environmental and social studies. A credit rating report put its operating income at 278.8 crore rupees in the 2017-18 financial year.

NTPC Limited.desc: India's state-controlled electricity generation company, with the Government of India holding 51.10 per cent of its equity. The government gave it Maharatna status in May 2010 and its shares have been listed since November 2004, after an offering the month before. It generates from coal and gas and has moved into hydro, renewable and nuclear generation; its own figures put it at 17 per cent of India's total national power capacity as of 31 March 2026.
